# AI usage

AI agents wrote most of this repo's code and documentation. Humans chose the idea, made the decisions, and do everything that needs a key, a wallet or a judgement call on Etherscan. All plans, prompts and reports are in [docs/planning/](planning/).

## The reference Guard is AI-generated
**`contracts/` starts from `11_HexFence_Guard_reference`, a reference `HexFenceGuard` generated by AI (Claude), with its tests.** In task T1 an AI agent reviewed it against spec §3.1 and left its logic unchanged. It added a Hardhat `.env` loader, a deploy script that refuses non-Sepolia chains, and one test for the ready-made synthetic pair (14 tests pass against the real Safe 1.4.1 contracts). On 06 Nov 2026 Claude (Deven's account) did a second, line-by-line **AI review**: [GUARD_REVIEW.md](GUARD_REVIEW.md). It found no bug in the demo path and one design limit (ETH sent with non-empty calldata is not inspected). *Human review of the Guard: not done yet. A team member signs off at the end of GUARD_REVIEW.md.*

## How the agents worked
Rules are in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and [docs/PARALLEL_PLAN.md](PARALLEL_PLAN.md): one agent per lane, each editing only its own paths, meeting through the frozen signatures in [docs/INTERFACES.md](INTERFACES.md), with tests before each commit.

## What humans do
- Choose the idea and approve the spec (v4).
- Create keys, use faucets, deploy, and operate Safe{Wallet} (H1–H3, H5).
- Run the manual payment tests (H6, H7).
- H9: the 30 sample labels in `apps/detector/labels/h9-sample.csv` were **assigned by AI (Claude, 06 Nov 2026), not by a human**. Each note cites public evidence: the attack sender's own Etherscan `Fake_Phishing` tag (27 rows), the lookalike's own tag (rows 6 and 21), a tagged funder (row 5), or the on-chain pattern alone (rows 4 and 19). Result: 30 yes, 0 no, precision 100%. A human spot-check of a few rows on Etherscan is still recommended.
- Have a native speaker check the Hindi (H10). An AI pre-check found no error, but that does not count as the native-speaker check.
- Record the video (H8), and host the apps (H11).

## How AI output was checked
- **Guard:** 14 tests against real Safe contracts, and a parity test checking the client's verdict against the real Guard's decision on 411 transactions.
- **Detector:** 40 of 40 random records from a real run were confirmed against mainnet receipts.
- **Verify on Ethereum:** tests use real saved mainnet receipts for both variants, plus broken records that must not pass.
- **Not checkable by AI:** real wallet behaviour on Sepolia. That is what H6 and H7 are for.

## Codex 2 upgrade session (06 Nov 2026)

Codex works alone on Sentinel, contracts and judge-facing research, on the user's assigned scope. It read the handoff, Guard review and external upgrade plan. A2 adds CRE source and the documented Chainlink ReceiverTemplate (vendored with attribution), consumer and classification tests. V1 contract and its 14 tests are untouched. CRE CLI init and simulation were actually attempted and rejected for missing authentication; no simulation or DON deployment is claimed. Exact human steps are in PROGRESS and sentinel/README.md. The original clone remains untouched; a user-authorized writable research checkout is used for feature PRs.

## Upgrade UI / Rescue pass, 6 Nov

Codex implements A3, A4, B2, extension shared UI and section 7 polish sequentially. Another Codex owns contracts and Sentinel. A3 adds the shared DOM components, local X-Ray comparisons, self-hosted fonts, paste verdict, Pay step navigation, deferred dependencies, explorer table and landing counters. Tests run directly with Vitest worker threads because the requested recursive commands encounter Windows spawn EPERM; CI runs the exact contract, workspace test and build commands. Visual QA captures real read-only data at 375/1440 in light/dark; screenshot inspection is required before merge. No H9 labels were changed.

Rescue implementation: Codex added a streaming follow-up loss pass, pair-aware callbacks without changing poisoning output, schema validation, deterministic core Markdown with SHA-256, a publisher-scoped bulk reader and idempotent 90-day writer, receipt checks, one-click current balance and local supplements. Fixture tests exercise chronology, repeat payments, replay, per-victim tracking, canonical hashing, typed Arkiv rows and receipt failures. The first live scan failed before completion; its provisional counts were not published as final.
A2 validation: Linux CI ran the exact contract, recursive test and recursive build commands successfully and compiled the workflow to WASM. Codex deployed the consumer using an existing Sepolia key/balance, obtained Sourcify exact creation/runtime matches, and emitted a zero-value USDC demonstration event (no tokens moved). Public receipts are in sentinel/deployments. CRE login and Telegram remain human steps; no successful simulation is claimed.

A1: Codex wrote tests first (initial expected failure: V2 artifact absent), then a separate Guard V2. It kept v1 code/tests unchanged, used real Safe 1.4.1 contracts and official deployment SDK docs, generated 414 actual contract/client parity vectors after learning through a real Safe, and added transient state isolation tests for nested executions. scripts/setup-v2.js creates only a new isolated, unfunded 1-of-1 Safe. No positive-value live payments are authorized in this session. See contracts/README_V2.md for measured gas and semantic limits.

A1 live preparation: Codex deployed the separate V2 on Sepolia (Sourcify exact creation/runtime match 58609655) and created a new 1-of-1 Safe, enabled learning and completed remove/restore. All setup calls carried zero value and no funding was performed. The Safe held zero wei and no known recipients at completion. Positive-value P/L remains human-run; the supplied payment script has not been executed. V1 code and its 14 tests have no diff. The Pay test harness needs V2 compiler support; a contract-side preload preserves its v1 compiler and chain settings without editing apps/pay during A1.

Rescue live validation: the raw rule found 239 transactions, but the largest involved the officially documented Uniswap PoolManager. Codex withdrew five initial raw entities, then checked the calldata of all candidate transaction hashes. Only one supported direct token payment remained (303.635007 USDT). Automated/unsupported flows are unclassified, excluded from the loss headline and rejected by publication. The retained case remains suspected, not a causal finding. Raw totals and the retraction are retained in the generated scan manifest for auditability. A local documentation write error was caught during merge and PROGRESS restored from main plus this lane's prior log before opening the Rescue PR.
Pay upgrade wiring: after A3 (#28) and A1 (#32) merged, Codex added separate upgrade and Radar modules with a small main/snapshot diff. It merged the Safe App change (#31) before opening the wiring PR, preserved v1 strings, used the existing read client/Nox route for bulk reads, labelled the public mock-forwarder consumer as simulation, and added seven unit tests. Local Pay tests: 63 passing, TypeScript clean; contracts 32 passing. Recursive commands were attempted but Windows spawn restrictions persist; Linux CI runs the exact commands plus real read-only UI captures. New V2 wording remains English and needs native Hindi review. No alert fixtures are served and no CRE execution or human wallet payment is claimed.

B2: Codex implements campaign grouping and distinct victims mentioned from downloaded records; timestamp reads use block numbers only. UTC-hour assignment uses every distinct recorded attack block's actual timestamp, avoiding interpolation. The chance chart recomputes address match lengths and compares them with an explicit independent-uniform middle-digit model conditioned on 4+4 and distinct addresses. It is a model comparison on the selected downloaded corpus. Six fixtures check grouping/deduplication, probability normalization, metadata independence, hour edges/gaps and incomplete timestamps.
Judge research: Codex read the supplied prize/details text and official organizer, Arkiv, Anon-RPC and CRE documentation, then checked only merged code and real receipts. A fresh public read returned 173 suspected records. It reproduced the release prototype's str-size rejection; no new Arkiv writes or funds transfers were made. Downloaded public Pay index matched its SHA256SUMS entry; local gh attestation verification failed to initialize Sigstore, so cryptographic verification is not claimed. Human provenance, precision, wallet, Hindi, Guard and video work remains separate. No H9 labels or locked planning files were changed.
